# CloudNativePG

Plugin ID `cnpg`. CloudNativePG Postgres clusters and the age of their last backup.

A panel on the Storage page lists the CloudNativePG clusters with their state and the age of their
last available backup. The clusters come from the cluster through the kubernetes plugin; the
backup age comes from `plugins.cnpg.backupMetric` through the prometheus plugin, and without it
the clusters are listed with no age. The plugin is `unavailable` on a cluster without the
CloudNativePG CRD.

## What it shows

### Pages

No page of its own.

### Panels on other pages

| Page | Panel | Id |
|---|---|---|
| Storage (`storage`) | Postgres clusters (CNPG) | `cnpg` |

### Topics

Published on `/api/v1/stream` and `/api/v1/topics/{topic}`:

| Topic | Payload | What |
|---|---|---|
| `cnpg.clusters` | `CNPGClustersData` | The CloudNativePG clusters with their instances, phase and last backup age. |

## Dependencies

A change to a plugin's settings restarts it and the plugins that require or use it.

- **Requires** [Kubernetes](kubernetes.md): while it does not run or is `unavailable`, this plugin is `blocked` and its pages are hidden.
- **Uses** [Prometheus-compatible](prometheus.md) when it runs.

## Settings

Every setting is under `plugins.cnpg` in the config file and is also in the [configuration reference](../configuration.md#pluginscnpg), with the rules for all of them: the layers, the `_FILE` form of each variable and secret references. _Restart_ marks a setting that applies only when dash restarts; a change to any other restarts the plugin in place.

| Setting | Variable | Type | Default | Secret | Restart | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plugins.cnpg.type` | `DASH_PLUGINS_CNPG_TYPE` | string | - | no | no | The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name. |
| `plugins.cnpg.enabled` | `DASH_PLUGINS_CNPG_ENABLED` | boolean | - | no | no | false turns the plugin off: its topics are removed, and the web UI drops its rail entry, palette entries, overview tiles and panels and shows a switched-off page at its address. Unset turns it on when it has the settings it needs (rustfs is off unless enabled: true, because nothing in its settings says an object store exists); a plugin without them is disabled ("not configured: set plugins.<id>.url", naming the setting to make) and the web UI hides its pages. true with settings missing or invalid makes it unconfigured, which hides its pages too. This is how prometheus, alertmanager, gatus, victorialogs, proxmox, hardware, ssh, kubernetes, flux, cnpg, rustfs, grafana, headlamp and launcher behave, and a change to any of their settings applies live: that plugin restarts, and so do the plugins that use or require it (a prometheus change restarts proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, cnpg and rustfs; a gatus change restarts hardware and kubernetes; a proxmox change restarts hardware; a kubernetes change restarts proxmox, flux and cnpg; a grafana change restarts alertmanager). |
| `plugins.cnpg.backupMetric` | `DASH_PLUGINS_CNPG_BACKUP_METRIC` | string | `barman_cloud_cloudnative_pg_io_last_available_backup_timestamp` | no | no | Name of the Prometheus series that holds the Unix time of a cluster's last available backup, labelled namespace and cluster (role="primary" selects the primary's). The default is the Barman Cloud plugin's barman_cloud_cloudnative_pg_io_last_available_backup_timestamp. Must be a valid metric name. |

The cnpg plugin reads the newest sample of `plugins.cnpg.backupMetric` per cluster with
`role="primary"` for the age shown on the Storage page. Without the prometheus plugin the
clusters are listed with a `prometheus: not_configured` note and no age.

## Actions

None: the plugin only reads.

## Kubernetes RBAC

dash reads the cluster with its ServiceAccount. The Helm chart grants each group of rules below while the value named is set ([RBAC modes](../deploy/kubernetes.md#rbac-modes)); with `rbac.create: false`, grant them yourself.

**To read the CloudNativePG clusters** (chart: `rbac.read`), in the ClusterRole:

```yaml
rules:
  - apiGroups: [postgresql.cnpg.io]
    resources: [clusters]
    verbs: [get, list, watch]
```

The cnpg plugin reads the CloudNativePG clusters with the same ServiceAccount as the kubernetes
plugin; a refusal shows on the cnpg row, not on the kubernetes one.

## Demo twin

With `DASH_DEMO=true` dash runs the plugin's demo twin instead: the same manifest, enabled and configured whatever the settings say, publishing made-up data from the fake lab in `internal/demo/world` and contacting nothing.
